title: Sifat in our ayat: practising the qualities in Al-Inshiqaq: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Inshiqaq and the sifat of strength
source: Written for quran/y6 lesson 13 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Sifat in our ayat rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 13. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Peer listening in pairs
points: Name one word and one quality

keywords.def: the qualities of a letter's sound (singular sifah)
a bounce on ق ط ب ج د with sukoon

questions.q: Recite 84:1 to 2 and say every sifat you hear on the last letter of each ayah.
questions.a: ٱنشَقَّتْ: ت hams, breath; وَحُقَّتْ: ت hams, breath.

questions.q: Breakout pairs: recite 84:1 to 15 to each other and write one sifat correction for your partner on the pupil PDF. Today's rota group recites to the teacher.
questions.a: Each pupil gets one precise correction, e.g. 'breath on ت in 84:2'.

questions.q: Extend: find a qalqalah letter in 84:16.
questions.a: ق in أُقْسِمُ, and ق at the end of ٱلشَّفَقِ when stopping.

questions.q: Stretch: which is strongest, a qalqalah letter in the middle of a word or at a stop?
questions.a: At a stop (the bounce is strongest at the end of an ayah).
A) raised (isti'la) and whispered (hams). ص is a heavy (isti'la) letter and in the hams phrase (شَخْصٌ).

questions.q: Think again: A good reciter is like a careful builder. Which 'brick' (letter quality) do you most often get wrong?
questions.a: Often the breath on ت, or adding a vowel after a qalqalah letter. Naming it helps us fix it.
